title: `DOUBLE % DOUBLE`
verdict: no option matches: NaN for a zero divisor or an infinite dividend
description: NaN for a zero divisor or an infinite dividend (duckdb-R4).
Round 4 (probes): FLOAT `%` is a FLOAT and truncates like `fmod` (`-7 % 3 = -1`, `7 % -3 = 1`, `-7.5 % 2 = -1.5`); `1 % 0` and `inf % 1` are NaN.

The numeric functions page says `%` raises on a zero divisor, which FLOAT and DOUBLE `%` do not: a docs bug, DD-8. The page is also silent on `%` of doubles truncating while its `fmod` floors (`-7.5::DOUBLE % 2` is -1.5, `fmod(-7.5, 2)` 0.5): a docs gap. No upstream test pins the sign of a negative dividend's `%` on doubles; it may change between versions.
reference: `modulus` of doubles is `fmod` (duckdb-R4); a zero divisor and an infinite dividend raise.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).

evidence.note: ModuloOperator<float>, <double>: std::fmod, truncating, NaN for a zero divisor or an infinite dividend
% of FLOAT and of DOUBLE: BindBinaryFloatingPoint<ModuloOperator>
the SQL function fmod is a macro, x - y * floor(x / y): floored, and inexact
fmod: the floored definition, always DOUBLE

provenance.notes: `%` on FLOAT is `std::fmod` at float, as on DOUBLE. The function named `fmod` is a different thing: a macro that floors (`fmod(-7.5, 2) = 0.5`, where `-7.5 % 2 = -1.5`) and computes through `/`, `*`, `floor` and `-`, so it rounds. The docs describe that macro correctly; facts that call `%` C's fmod mean `std::fmod`. The lift reads only `%` as `sverify_fmod`.

evidence.note: CompareValues: numeric results are cast to the column type and compared with Value::ValuesAreEqual
ApproxEqual: NaN equals NaN, non-finite values compare exactly, finite ones within 1 %

provenance.notes: No test takes `%` of a negative FLOAT or DOUBLE, so `division_type` at fp32 stays at the source reading. The runner compares FLOAT and DOUBLE results within 1 % and counts NaN equal to NaN of either sign and `-0.0` equal to `0.0` (`test/sqlite/result_helper.cpp`, `ApproxEqual` in `src/common/types.cpp`); infinities, integers, booleans and strings compare exactly.
